headlines: MIAMI-DADE COUNTY NOW ACCEPTS BITCOIN FOR PROPERTY TAXES
PAY MIAMI-DADE PROPERTY TAXES WITH BITCOIN
MIAMI-DADE LEADS NATION BY ACCEPTING BITCOIN FOR TAXES
draft.article:
Miami-Dade property owners can now settle their property tax bills using Bitcoin. Miami-Dade County Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez shared the announcement on Monday, confirming that the digital currency is officially being accepted.

Residents can use the cryptocurrency option for their property tax payments through online portals or directly in person at the tax collector office.

The new rollout places Miami-Dade County among the first public government entities across the United States to take Bitcoin for tax payments, expanding how local taxpayers can clear their official county bills.

items.desc: A judge kept Miami-Dade’s elections chief on the recount board despite a lawsuit calling her Rep. María Elvira Salazar’s “political ally” and friend.

headlines: RECOUNT UNDERWAY IN MIAMI DISTRICT 27 CONGRESSIONAL RACE
JUDGE KEEPS MIAMI-DADE ELECTIONS CHIEF ON RECOUNT BOARD
MIAMI AND CORAL GABLES RACE FACES HEATED RECOUNT BATTLE
draft.article:
A recount is officially underway across Florida's 27th Congressional District, covering parts of Miami and Coral Gables, after a razor-thin election contest between Republican Representative María Elvira Salazar and Democrat Eliott Rodriguez.

Miami-Dade's elections chief remains on the oversight board for the recount after a judge rejected a lawsuit challenging her participation. The court filing had alleged a conflict of interest, describing the elections administrator as a personal friend and political ally of Salazar.

Salazar publicly declared victory on Tuesday in the heavily Hispanic South Florida district. However, the Associated Press has not officially called the race as recount procedures continue.

headlines: HIALEAH MOTHER CHARGED AFTER CHILD FOUND CHAINED TO FENCE
BODYCAM REVEALS HIALEAH CHILD CHAINED OUTSIDE
WHAT HIALEAH POLICE DISCOVERED CHAINED OUTSIDE A RESIDENCE
draft.article: Hialeah Police released body camera footage showing officers discovering a 13-year-old special needs girl secured to a fence with a metal chain. The incident occurred on July 11 near 355 West 63rd Street and Fourth Avenue in Hialeah. Authorities stated that 34-year-old Yashira Maldonado wrapped the chain around her daughter's waist after being fired from her job. Maldonado then placed her phone on silent, went home, and watched television in bed. The child was left alongside a backpack and shoes. The victim's great-grandmother found her and dialed 911 after failing to untie the chain. Maldonado faces felony child abuse and neglect charges and has bonded out of jail.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE FIRE RESCUE REQUESTS $2.9 MILLION FOR HELICOPTER REPAIRS
SALTWATER DAMAGE SQUEEZES MIAMI-DADE RESCUE HELICOPTER BUDGET
WHY MIAMI RESCUE HELICOPTERS NEED MILLIONS IN SALTWATER REPAIRS
draft.article: Miami-Dade Fire Rescue is seeking county approval to spend an extra $2.9 million to maintain its Air Rescue fleet. Excessive corrosion driven by local humidity and saltwater intrusion has accelerated wear on the helicopters, which were bought in November 2019. Assistant Fire Chief Rick Rojas explained that Miami's coastal climate creates unique repair challenges for the department's four Leonardo AW139 helicopters. Unplanned radio work and aircraft incidents have depleted the bureau's original $6.66 million budget faster than expected. The county's Safety and Health Committee unanimously approved the resolution, which raises the repair allocation to $9.56 million. A full commission vote is scheduled for January 20.

headlines: 70-YEAR-OLD FELON ARRESTED FOR LEISURE CITY MOTEL STABBING
PROBATION VIOLATOR JAILED AFTER MOTEL ATTACK
CONVICTED FELON ON PROBATION BACK IN MIAMI-DADE JAIL
draft.article: Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office deputies arrested 70-year-old Vernon Tillman on Sunday morning following a stabbing at the Yes Motel in Leisure City. Deputies arrived around 7 a.m. at the property, located at 28475 South Dixie Highway. Investigators reported Tillman attacked a woman with a small knife after she finished showering, inflicting head wounds that required staples. Tillman was booked into the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center before 9:30 a.m. on Sunday, where he remains held without bond. State records show Tillman was on probation until January 2029 for prior armed robbery and armed carjacking convictions. He now faces an aggravated battery charge before Miami-Dade Circuit Judge Ramiro Areces.

headlines: CANALS BEGAN DRAINING THE FLORIDA EVERGLADES IN 1906
1906: EVERGLADES WATER REMOVAL CANALS BEGAN
WHEN CANALS BEGAN DRAINING THE FLORIDA EVERGLADES IN 1906
draft.article: In 1906, a transformative chapter began right in our South Florida backyard when canals were begun to remove water from the Florida Everglades. This landmark effort in 1906 marked the exact period when canals began draining the Everglades, redirecting water away from the vast wetland environment. The construction of these water removal channels in 1906 permanently initiated the drainage of the Florida Everglades, setting off decades of change for the local landscape and waterways that surround the Miami area today.
